diagram_classification: theological (Trinitarian diagram, a variant of the Scutum Fidei or Shield of the Trinity, with a crucifixion figure)
interpretation: The diagram expresses the doctrine of the Trinity. Three outer roundels, which seem to read PATER, SPIRITUS SANCTUS and FILIUS, sit at the corners of an inverted triangle. A central roundel reads DEUS. Short bands run from DEUS to each of the three Persons and carry the word EST (is). The three sides of the triangle connect the Persons to one another and carry NON EST (is not). The diagram therefore says that the Father is God, the Son is God and the Holy Spirit is God, while the Father is not the Son, the Son is not the Spirit and the Spirit is not the Father. The Persons are distinct, yet each is the one divine essence. The crucified Christ is drawn on the vertical axis between DEUS and FILIUS. This links the Son's incarnation and sacrifice to the divine unity and marks the Son as the Person who became visible and human. The faint circular, wheel-like drawing behind the triangle seems to be a show-through from the other side of the leaf or an earlier design. It is not part of this diagram and is left uninterpreted.
evidence: Visible: three corner roundels with names (PATER and FILIUS are legible, and the third is probably SPIRITUS SANCTUS); a central roundel marked DEUS; the inner connecting bands labelled EST; the outer triangle sides labelled NON EST; a crucified figure placed between DEUS and FILIUS. External: this EST / NON EST scheme is the standard medieval Trinitarian diagram (the Scutum Fidei), which became common in the 12th and 13th centuries, and the crucifixion variant fits that tradition. The identification of the third roundel and of the background drawing is less certain because of the damage and show-through.
